newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products steady to higher Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products steady to higher Tuesday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices were steady to higher Tuesday, as talk of Northwest refinery problems and upcoming turnarounds drew buyers, traders said.

Traders said Tosco Corp would restart its 95,000 barrel-per-day refinery late today in Ferndale, Wash., after weekend storms battered the plant's power supply and forced it off-line by Monday. Other plants also had problems, traders said.
"Between the refinery problems and lower inventories, that's driving prices up," a trader claimed.
Upgrades of major units, such Unocal's Wilmington, Calif., coker and Mobil's crude unit, could also tighten supplies in coming months, traders said.
Los Angeles conventional gasoline rose 0.50 cents a gallon from Monday to 76/77 cents gallon, while CARB grade remained flat on the day.
Los Angeles jet fuel saw bids and offers rise two cents to 82/83 cents a gallon Tuesday.
